temperatures. When these chemicals react they form iodine. Sodium thiosulfate solution and starch
solution can be used to show how fast the reaction proceeds.
Read all the instructions carefully before starting the experiments.

tests on solid P
Divide solid P into three portions.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Place the first portion of solid P in a boiling tube. Add a small piece of aluminium foil and
about 2cm of aqueous sodium hydroxide to the boiling tube. Heat the mixture and test the
gas produced with indicator paper.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Use your results from (b)(i) to identify the gas produced.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Place the second portion of solid P in a test-tube. Add about 2cm of distilled water to the
test-tube. Stopper and shake the test-tube to dissolve solid P. Add a few drops of dilute
nitric acid and about 1cm of aqueous barium nitrate.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: What conclusion can you draw about solid P from your observations in (c)(i)?

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Do a flame test on the third portion of solid P.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
Identify solid P.

tests on solid Q

parts.label: (f)
parts.text:
Heat about half of solid Q in a hard glass test-tube.
Record your observations.

Add about 4cm of distilled water to the rest of solid Q in a test-tube. Stopper and shake the
test-tube to dissolve solid Q.
Divide the solution into two equal portions in two test-tubes.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Add an excess of aqueous sodium hydroxide to the first portion of the solution. Leave the
mixture to stand for approximately 5 minutes.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Add a few drops of dilute nitric acid and about 1cm of aqueous silver nitrate to the second
portion of the solution.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (h)
parts.text: What conclusions can you draw about the identity of solid Q?
